criteria.criterion: A test on the cutover fixture creates a PR branch after C0 with a records-only commit, a declared-intervention commit and a verified job-landing commit, none named by a landing record. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli` (the new history test): `athena check --history` on that head reports no violations.
criteria.evidence: The test a_pr_head_of_records_only_intervention_and_job_landing_commits_passes passed. It lands a job with `go` on branch `pr`, adds a PRIVATE.md commit and an intervention commit, asserts that no landing record names any of them (cutover_commit_at gives None), and checks that `athena check --history` succeeds with '0 violation(s)'. On the base, all post-C0 commits went to attribution, so this test would fail there.

criteria.criterion: A test adds a governed-content change with no verification or intervention to a PR branch after C0. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli` (the new history test): `athena check --history` fails and the violation names that commit's sha.
criteria.evidence: The test a_pr_head_with_an_unverified_governed_change_fails_naming_it passed. It asserts that the check fails, that the output contains the bad commit's 12-character sha and 'changes governed content', that it does not name the records-only commit, and that it does not contain 'unattributed'.

criteria.criterion: A test shows `athena check --history` on the fixture's main after C0 gives the same report as before: commits on main still go through the attribution rule, and an unattributed commit on main still fails. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate -p athena-cli`.
criteria.evidence: history_on_main_after_c0_still_judges_its_commits_by_attribution passed. On main, a records-only commit and a governed hand commit are both reported as 'unattributed', never with the pre-merge wording. The existing test the_history_and_attribution_checks_pass_on_the_fixtures_main passed, as did all 20 gate history tests, including the existing cutover_tests attribution case.

criteria.criterion: All existing history and attribution tests and the land.rs pr_commits tests pass unchanged. Run `cargo test --workspace`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records for this tree: fmt passed, clippy passed, and the tests passed (1187 ran). The diff changes no existing test file or assertion. I ran the 13 land::tests myself (classification and refusal cases) and all passed.

criteria.criterion: The CI history job in .github/workflows/ci.yml has the refs it needs on a pull_request event (main, and athena/records where used) so the merge base resolves. The step comments say why. The job keeps the name 'the full history'.
criteria.evidence: Checked by reading the diff. The step skip `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` is removed, and the step now runs `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main athena/records:athena/records`. The job and step comments explain the merge-base split and why both refs are needed. `name: the full history` is unchanged. CI itself cannot run in this snapshot.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry that says a PR head's own commits after C0 are judged by the pre-merge rule and main's by attribution, and cites the PR #175 failure.
criteria.evidence: The new 'Fixed' entry says this, cites PR #175 with its 50 violations and the quoted message, and mentions the fallback note, the classifier move and the CI fetch.

criteria.criterion: The pre-merge classifier has one source of truth in the gate; land.rs pr_commits delegates to it, with no duplicated rule logic.
criteria.evidence: The closing_jobs, JobFiles verification, added_interventions and fingerprint branches were removed from land.rs and now exist only in `invariant::classify_pre_merge`. land.rs calls it and maps `Uncovered::clause()` into its existing error text. The history check calls the same function.

findings.summary: A merge commit on a PR head (main merged into the branch) is judged by the pre-merge rule against its first parent, so main's governed changes it brings in would be reported as 'changes governed content'.
findings.evidence: Found by reading the code; no test covers it. `rev-list` includes merge commits, and classify_pre_merge diffs against the first parent. land::pr_commits behaves the same way, so the two are consistent, but a PR updated by merging main may fail the history check.

findings.summary: The planned gate unit test in history.rs for the path where the tip is an ancestor of main was not added; only the CLI test covers the on-main path.
findings.evidence: The diff adds no test in history.rs. The CLI test history_on_main_after_c0_still_judges_its_commits_by_attribution covers the behaviour.

findings.summary: The CI acceptance item (the history job passes on a real pull request) cannot be shown from this snapshot.
findings.evidence: There is no remote and CI cannot run here. The merge-base logic CI relies on is covered by the fixture tests, which use refs/remotes/origin/main the same way CI fetches it.

summary: The change fixes the cause in the history check itself. In `check_after_cutover`, a head that main does not hold is now split at its merge base with main. The commits after the merge base go to the pre-merge rule, now `invariant::classify_pre_merge`, its single source in the gate. Everything up to the merge base still goes to attribution. A head that is main or part of it keeps today's behaviour, and a checkout with no main or no usable merge base falls back to today's behaviour and adds a note. `land::classify_commit` now calls the gate classifier and keeps its messages; all 13 existing `land::tests` pass unchanged. I ran the new tests in `history_pr_head.rs` against the real binary on the cutover fixture. They show three things: a PR branch of a job landing, a records-only commit and an intervention passes with 0 violations; a hand-made governed change fails, naming its sha; and on main, records-only and hand commits are still reported as unattributed. The existing cutover and history tests still pass. The CI history job now fetches main and athena/records on every event, the step comments say why, and the job keeps its name. CHANGELOG.md cites PR #175's 50 violations. I could not run CI on a real pull request from this snapshot. The issues I found are minor: a planned gate unit test is missing, and merge commits on a PR branch are unhandled.
